hypotheses.claim: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 500 ms, a stagnation-adaptive ruin score that switches from pure worst-cost removal (low iter_frac, low stagnation) to a relatedness + near-full-route-load gated removal (high iter_frac / stagnation) will reduce mean objective below the current SBS 15.7807, because the archive's weakest regimes (capacity_level=tight -23.6%, depot_style=eccentric -21.0%, spatial=clustered -20.3%) indicate the current fixed priority under-diversifies exactly where ruin-set composition matters most, and relatedness-based destroy sets raise the probability that Regret-2 reinsertion finds improving recombinations instead of re-creating the removed pattern.

next_search_advice.direction: Improve `score_ruin_nodes` by making the ruin priority a stagnation-adaptive, rank-power-mixed score: multiply normalized removal savings by (a) a tight-capacity load gate that favours customers on near-full routes (weakest regime = capacity_level tight, gap -23.6%), (b) an eccentric-depot radial gate that favours extreme-radius customers (weakest regime = depot_style eccentric, gap -21.0%), and (c) blend with a Shaw-style spatial-cluster relatedness term when stagnation_ratio grows, so destroy sets shift from "worst-cost" (early, iter_frac<0.3) to "related cluster + high-load" (late, stagnating). Rank-power exponent p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio) interpolates from p≈1.0 early to p≈3.0 under stagnation, with deterministic index-based tie-breaking.
